passage:
I’m Deepika, and I sit behind Tushar in class, so I saw his phone all last week. He and half the boys are in a fan war against the followers of another actor. At first it was only jokes and funny edits, and Tushar laughed so hard he wheezed.
Then the comments changed. He typed something nasty under a rival fan’s photo, and the group chat filled with cheering replies. Imran, sitting beside him, did not reply at all and just kept scrolling.
Tushar looked thrilled, as if he were on a team in a real match. Later the rival fan wrote, “Why are you all so mean?” Tushar went quiet. I can’t know what he felt, but he locked his phone.

qa.q: How did the fan war begin, according to Deepika?
qa.a: It began as jokes and funny edits, and Tushar laughed so hard he wheezed.

qa.q: What might Tushar have felt when the group chat cheered his nasty line?
qa.a: He may have felt thrilled and part of a team, since he looked as if he were in a real match. The cheering rewarded him for going further.

qa.q: What could Tushar try when the banter starts to hurt someone?
qa.a: He could stop typing and picture the rival fan reading the words. Then he could decide whether the line is still a joke or has turned into cruelty.

qa.q: How might Imran, who kept scrolling, have seen the fight?
qa.a: Imran may have felt uneasy about the cruelty but did not want to break the group's mood. The passage shows only that he did not reply, so his reason is a guess.

grounding: Shows a teenage fan joining a fan war that slides from joking into cruelty, seen through an observer's account.

passage:
Monday. Sahil’s group of school friends posted jokes about a rival star’s new film, and rival fans posted jokes back. Sahil laughed at every reply and felt part of a team.
Wednesday. The jokes got sharper. Sahil posted an edited photo mocking how a rival fan looked, and the chat filled with “savage” and “more!” Chetan did not reply.
Friday. The rival fan, a girl, wrote, “I thought this was about films.” Sahil’s stomach dropped. He typed a mean answer, then deleted it. Chetan sent him a private message: “Bro, that one went too far.”
Sahil looked at the message for a long time, then took the photo down.

qa.q: What did the rival fan write on Friday?
qa.a: The rival fan wrote, “I thought this was about films.”

qa.q: Why did Sahil delete the mean answer he had typed?
qa.a: Sahil's stomach dropped when he saw that the rival fan was hurt. The cheering had made him feel like part of a team, but her message made him see a real person.

qa.q: What made Chetan's private message a good move?
qa.a: Chetan did not shame Sahil in front of the group. A short private message made it easier for Sahil to step back.

qa.q: How might the rival fan have felt seeing the edited photo and the cheering replies?
qa.a: She was likely hurt and outnumbered. Her reply, that she thought it was about films, shows she expected fun and got mockery instead.

grounding: Shows a teenager enjoying a fan war with friends as banter turns into cruelty, and then noticing the harm.
